subject: How to format y-axis numbers after sqrt transformation?

messages.author: f5bec70b36df06aa
messages.subject: How to format y-axis numbers after sqrt transformation?
parts:
HI @all

I am having another problem with a facetted dot plot. I had to
transform my y-axis due to outliers but now I don't know how to round
those numbers to 2 digits (the labels on the y-axis). I tried the
following:

read.csv("http://dl.dropbox.com/u/4236038/new_files/
nutrients_new_sw.csv") -> nutrients_sw

melt_nutrients_sw <- melt(nutrients_sw, id=c("ID", "round", "Season",
"catchment"),
na.rm=TRUE)

melt_nutrients_sw$ID <- factor(melt_nutrients_sw$ID,
levels=c(5,9,10,12,15,14,17,18,19,22,20,1,4,54,50,49,48,43,46,39,38,37,32,33,35,21,23))
melt_nutrients_sw$value <- signif(melt_nutrients_sw$value, digits = 1)
p <- ggplot(melt_nutrients_sw, aes(x = ID, y = value, color =
Season))
p + geom_point() + facet_grid(variable~catchment, scales = "free") +
scale_y_sqrt()

Any ideas?
Thanks, Martin (again)

with ggplot you can specify an optional function to format your axis
labels.

my.round <- function(x){
round(x,2)
}

p <- ggplot(melt_nutrients_sw, aes(x = ID, y = value, color=Season)) +
